subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should SMS webhook ingress accept the proposed 300/min failed-request budget with rejection deferred until the request is known invalid, so valid signed callbacks retain their separate 30/min dispatch capacity?
rationale: Source, tests, docs, and CI support the implementation, but choosing how much unauthenticated parsing and validation work to tolerate in exchange for avoiding callback starvation is a security and availability policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept the two-stage boundary
options.body: Merge the current design with a 300/min invalid-request budget and an independent 30/min dispatch cap per account route and resolved client.

options.title: Retune before merge
options.body: Choose a different failed-request threshold or add another generic ingress guard if the current pre-authentication work allowance is too permissive.

options.title: Keep the existing boundary
options.body: Decline the change and retain the shared 30/min pre-validation limit, accepting that invalid same-key traffic can block later valid callbacks.

recommendation.title: Accept the two-stage boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the current design with a 300/min invalid-request budget and an independent 30/min dispatch cap per account route and resolved client.

likelyOwner.reason: The original SMS webhook author and recent merger of adjacent webhook hardening is the strongest available owner for this security-versus-availability boundary.
